title: Successor graph activation at predecessor epoch + 1
description:
Objective: close the one gap the graph supersession transition deliberately left open — a SUCCESSOR graph revision cannot currently activate at predecessor epoch + 1, so a superseded chain's second generation would re-activate at epoch 1 and the monotonic-epoch guarantee holds only for the emitted binding, never for the successor's own durable state.

Hard dependencies: Graph revision supersession transition (task-1df0622e87cf42beae2cd82280e9ff99). Nothing here is plannable until that task is DONE and `graphEpoch` exists on `GraphRevisionState` on disk.

*** MEASURED ON DISK 2026-08-09 at HEAD 025dc4948127e7c7b753b71d3f5cf4b142637060 by architect-8ee37119. Re-measure before planning; these claims are stale by default. ***

THE EPOCH AUTHORITY IS REAL AND ALREADY LANDED — do not mint a second one. The goal aggregate owns it exactly as `graph-revision-reducer.ts:5-7` claims:
- `goal-contract.ts:130,155` — `readonly graphEpoch: number` on goal state and on the activation event.
- `goal-reducer.ts:94` — `goal.create` seeds `graphEpoch: 0` on DRAFT.
- `goal-reducer.ts:110` — `goal.activate_initial_graph` sets `graphEpoch: state.graphEpoch + 1`.
- `goal-reducer.ts:113` — emits `GoalExecutionEnabled` CARRYING `graphEpoch`, so the wire that hands the epoch to a revision already exists.
- `goal-validation.ts:228-238` — validates it: safe integer, `>= 0`, DRAFT implies 0, COMPLETED implies > 0, active implies > 0.

THE ACTUAL GAP, both halves measured:
1. GOAL SIDE — `goal-reducer.ts:40` admits `goal.activate_initial_graph` from `DRAFT` ONLY. There is no command that advances a goal's `graphEpoch` a second time, so in practice the epoch can only ever be 0 or 1. Supersession needs an epoch advance admitted from the live execution lifecycle that increments `graphEpoch` and rebinds `activeGraphRevisionRef` to the successor revision.
2. GRAPH REVISION SIDE — the supersession transition task sets `graphEpoch: 1` literally when a revision activates (its DoD 1 says "initial activation establishes epoch 1"). A successor therefore cannot land at N+1. The activation path must instead bind the goal-issued epoch: it has to arrive on the command and be validated against the predecessor it replaces, not be hardcoded.

WHY IT WAS DEFERRED, not an oversight: DoD 2 of task-1df0622e requires only that the accepted supersede result EMIT a binding to the successor at exactly epoch + 1, which it does via the kernel-produced `GraphRevisionSuperseded` event. Making the successor's own activation consume that binding reaches `GraphActivationBinding`, `bindingShape`, `sameBinding`, `BINDING_KEYS`, the approval/activation fixtures and both invariant driver suites — far past the 10-file cap for that task.

SIZING WARNING, measured: `goal-reducer.ts` is 247 physical lines and `goal-validation.ts` is 245, both effectively at the 250 target with no headroom, so this work almost certainly requires splitting a file rather than growing one. Note also that `planning-source-size.test.ts` sweeps `src/planning` ONLY — `packages/core/src/goal/` is NOT guarded and `goal-reducer.test.ts` already sits at 300 lines. Do not read a green core suite as proof of the per-file cap in `goal/`; hand-measure with `grep -c ''`.

CONTAINED: `packages/core/src/planning/planning-contract.ts` does NOT share `GraphActivationBinding` — the planning-run aggregate carries its own hash set — so the planning-run reducer and its fixtures are outside this blast radius.

Likely owned paths (verify by fresh grep): packages/core/src/goal/goal-contract.ts, goal-reducer.ts, goal-validation.ts, goal-reducer.test.ts, goal-invariants.test.ts, packages/core/src/planning/graph-revision-contract.ts, graph-revision-validation.ts, graph-revision-reducer.ts, graph-revision-test-fixtures.ts, graph-revision-reducer.test.ts.

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/core typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/core test
definitionOfDone: A goal-side epoch advance exists: a command admitted from the goal's live execution lifecycle (not only DRAFT) increments `graphEpoch` by exactly 1 and rebinds `activeGraphRevisionRef` to the named successor revision, composing the landed counter at goal-reducer.ts:110 rather than introducing a second epoch.

A graph revision activates at an epoch supplied by the goal aggregate instead of the literal 1: the activation path validates the incoming epoch against the predecessor it replaces, and an initial activation still lands at epoch 1 with every pre-active lifecycle at 0.

A successor revision produced by `graph.supersede` activates at exactly predecessor epoch + 1, proven end to end by a test that drives supersede then activates the successor and asserts the durable state epoch — not merely the emitted binding.

A stale, equal, skipped or non-integer epoch cannot activate a successor and cannot advance the goal; each refusal pins the exact stable @moe/contracts code and the refusing layer, and no parallel vocabulary is minted.

Every pre-existing assertion in goal-reducer.test.ts, goal-invariants.test.ts and graph-revision-reducer.test.ts passes unchanged except those the epoch binding genuinely invalidates, and a mutation drill proves each new epoch guard is reddenable.

Fresh `pnpm --filter @moe/core typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/core test` exits 0, and every touched production file is at or below 250 physical lines measured by `grep -c ''` — goal-reducer.ts (247) and goal-validation.ts (245) start with no headroom and will need splitting, not growing.
taskRails: Compose the landed goal epoch authority — goal-contract.ts:130/155, goal-reducer.ts:94/110/113, goal-validation.ts:228-238. Do not add a second epoch counter, and do not move epoch authority into the graph revision aggregate; that aggregate persists a BOUND REFERENCE to the epoch it was activated at, nothing more.

MEASURE BEFORE PLANNING: if the fresh grep shows this exceeds 10 distinct files or 12 plan steps, split at the goal/graph-revision seam rather than submitting an oversized plan — but a goal-side-only slice must name its consumer task, because a pure epoch advance with nothing binding it violates the composition clause.

packages/core/src/goal/ is NOT covered by planning-source-size.test.ts, so a green suite proves nothing about the per-file cap there. Hand-measure with `grep -c ''`; PowerShell Measure-Object -Line skips blank lines and reports headroom you do not have.

Refusal tests assert the exact stable reason code AND which layer refused, never merely that the operation failed. Note that @moe/contracts RuntimeError DROPS its validated `source`, so the layer must come from a production discriminant on the result — never from a test helper that reconstructs it.
An epoch that cannot be verified is UNKNOWN and refuses; it never defaults to 0, to 1, or to the predecessor's value.

implementationPlan.description: RED first (TDD). Create packages/core/src/planning/graph-revision-succession.test.ts driving the production reducer end to end — this is DoD 3 and it is the point of the task. The proof: build a revision, activate it at epoch 1, supersede it, read the `successor` binding off the emitted GraphRevisionSuperseded event, then create the SUCCESSOR revision, submit it, and activate it with a witness carrying that binding — finally asserting the successor's DURABLE state.graphEpoch === 2, not merely that the event said 2. That distinction is the whole DoD: today the emitted binding already says 2 and the durable state would say 1. Consume the real `SupersessionSuccessorBinding` off the event rather than hand-building it, so the test proves the emitted binding is actually usable by the next activation. Also cover, each pinning the exact code and the GRAPH_REVISION layer via the existing production `layer` discriminant: an initial activation (no succession binding) whose epoch is not exactly 1; a successor whose epoch is not exactly predecessor + 1 (test +0, +2 and -1); a succession binding naming THIS revision as its own predecessor; a non-integer, negative or missing epoch. Every refusal leaves input state byte-identical (JSON.stringify before/after). Keep at or below 250 lines.
implementationPlan.note:
RED first, confirmed by a real run: `npx vitest run --root . packages/core/src/planning/graph-revision-succession.test.ts` -> "Test Files 1 failed (1) / Tests 5 failed | 1 passed (6)", failing with `TypeError: successorActivation is not a function`. 175 physical lines by `grep -c ''`, under the 250 ceiling.

WHAT THE SUITE PROVES, and the one thing it deliberately does NOT do: every positive path drives the PRODUCTION reducer end to end. `supersede()` reduces `graph.supersede` on a live ACTIVE revision and takes `event.successor` off the emitted `GraphRevisionSuperseded` -- the real kernel-produced `SupersessionSuccessorBinding`, never a hand-built literal, so the test proves the emitted binding is actually consumable by the next activation. `draftSuccessor()` then builds the successor through `graph_revision.create` + `graph_revision.submit` rather than as a state literal, so the successor's identity and content hash come from the kernel binding.

THE ASSERTION THAT IS THE WHOLE POINT: `expect(next.graphEpoch).toBe(predecessorEpoch + 1)` reads the DURABLE reducer state, not the event. The event already carries epoch 2 at HEAD; only persisted state distinguishes a bound epoch from the hardcoded literal. A second assertion pins the literal 2 so the arithmetic cannot silently agree with itself, and the emitted `GraphRevisionActivated.witness` is asserted to deep-equal the witness so durable and emitted can never diverge.

REFUSALS, each pinning code AND layer via `expectError`/`expectIllegal` (both assert `result.layer === "GRAPH_REVISION"`, the production discriminant, because RuntimeError drops its validated source):
- initial activation at epoch 0/2/3/-1 -> ILLEGAL_TRANSITION from APPROVED, with a POSITIVE control asserting epoch 1 still activates.
- successor epoch at predecessor +0 / +2 / -1 -> ILLEGAL_TRANSITION from PENDING_APPROVAL.
- succession binding whose predecessorGraphEpoch is 0, -1 or 1.5, or whose hash/ref is malformed -> ILLEGAL_TRANSITION (5 cases, count asserted).
- succession naming this very revision as its own predecessor -> REVISION_REBOUND, paired with a positive control showing the same witness with the real predecessor id activates. That pairing is what stops the rebound case passing for the wrong reason.
- missing, non-integer, NaN and string epochs -> ILLEGAL_TRANSITION (4 cases, count asserted).

Every sweep asserts its own case count (`expect(cases).toBe(N)`, `expect(bindings).toHaveLength(5)`) so a sweep that silently generates zero cannot pass. Every refusal goes through `refusedActivation()`, which JSON.stringify-compares the input state before and after.

NOTE ON exactOptionalPropertyTypes: the missing-epoch case is built by rest-destructuring (`const { graphEpoch: _omitted, ...withoutEpoch } = witness`) because an explicit `graphEpoch: undefined` is a type error under that flag.

implementationPlan.description: Contract. In graph-revision-contract.ts add the epoch to the ACTIVATION WITNESS, deliberately NOT to the shared `GraphActivationBinding`. Measured reason: `sameBinding` and `bindingOf` iterate BINDING_KEYS (the five hashes plus expectedGoalVersion), so putting the epoch there would reach validBinding, bindingShape, every approval fixture and the planning-run witnesses — far past this task's file budget — while putting it on the witness reaches only ACTIVATION_KEYS and validActivation. Add `readonly graphEpoch: number` to `GraphRevisionActivationWitness`, and a new `GraphRevisionSuccessionBinding` carrying `predecessorGraphContentHash`, `predecessorGraphEpoch` and `predecessorRevisionId`, exposed as an OPTIONAL `succession?: GraphRevisionSuccessionBinding` on the witness. Absent succession means an initial activation; present means this revision replaces the named predecessor. Mirror the field names of the kernel's `SupersessionSuccessorBinding` so the event's binding maps across without translation — do not mint a differently-named parallel shape. Document in a comment that the epoch here remains a BOUND REFERENCE to goal-owned authority (goal-reducer.ts:110), never a counter this aggregate advances. Budget ~20 lines against 62 free.
implementationPlan.note:
Contract landed exactly where the plan measured it should go. `graphEpoch` and the optional `succession` are on `GraphRevisionActivationWitness`, NOT on the shared `GraphActivationBinding` -- re-verified the reason on disk before writing: graph-revision-validation.ts:20-22 defines BINDING_KEYS as the five hashes plus expectedGoalVersion, and :46-48 `sameBinding` / :50-55 `bindingOf` iterate exactly that tuple. Adding a field there would reach validBinding, bindingShape, APPROVAL, the planning-run witnesses and every approval fixture; adding it to the witness reaches only ACTIVATION_KEYS and validActivation. `sameBinding(binding, activation)` therefore keeps comparing the same six fields and ignores the two new ones, which is what keeps every pre-existing activation assertion valid.

Added `GraphRevisionSuccessionBinding` with predecessorGraphContentHash / predecessorGraphEpoch / predecessorRevisionId. Two of those three names are taken verbatim from the kernel's `SupersessionSuccessorBinding` (supersession-engine.ts:19-22), so the emitted event binding maps across with no translation layer and no parallel vocabulary. The third, `predecessorGraphEpoch`, is deliberately NOT in the kernel binding -- the kernel's successor carries only its OWN `graphEpoch`. It is documented in the interface comment as the extra fact that lets validation check `epoch + 1` from the command alone, without reaching for state the validator cannot see. Option-B (mirroring the kernel binding wholesale) was reconsidered and rejected here: without the predecessor's epoch in the binding, "exactly predecessor + 1" degenerates into a self-consistency check that proves nothing.

Documented on the field that the epoch stays a BOUND REFERENCE to goal-owned authority and that this aggregate never advances a counter -- the same language the landed state field at :105-110 uses, so the two doc comments agree rather than drift.

implementationPlan.description: Validation — put the rules HERE, not in the reducer, because validation.ts has 123 lines free and the reducer has 13. In graph-revision-validation.ts: `validActivation` currently uses `exact(value, ACTIVATION_KEYS)`, which rejects any extra key, so an optional field needs two key tuples exactly as planning-expansion-validation.ts:119-122 does with PROPOSE_KEYS / PROPOSE_PROOF_KEYS. Add ACTIVATION_KEYS + graphEpoch as the base tuple and a second tuple adding `succession`, accepting either shape. Add a `validSuccessionBinding` predicate (both hashes hex64, predecessorRevisionId a valid ref, predecessorGraphEpoch a safe integer >= 1) and fold the arithmetic in: with no succession the witness epoch must be EXACTLY 1; with succession it must be EXACTLY predecessorGraphEpoch + 1. A non-integer, negative, zero or absent epoch fails closed — never defaults. Keep the existing `validGraphEpochPlacement` at :94-101 untouched; it governs STATE placement and remains correct. Budget ~25 lines against 123 free.
implementationPlan.note:
All shape and arithmetic rules live here, none in the reducer -- the file has the headroom (127 -> 156 by `grep -c ''`, +29 against 123 free, still 94 free) and the reducer does not (13 free).

TWO KEY TUPLES, copying the measured precedent at planning-expansion-validation.ts:119-122. ACTIVATION_KEYS gains "graphEpoch"; SUCCESSION_ACTIVATION_KEYS = [...ACTIVATION_KEYS, "succession"]. `validActivation` now reads `if (!exact(value, ACTIVATION_KEYS) && !exact(value, SUCCESSION_ACTIVATION_KEYS)) return false;` -- both tuples narrow to the same Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>, and tsc accepts the narrowing after the compound guard (verified: `pnpm --filter @moe/core typecheck` reports zero errors in this file). This is the risk the plan flagged as easiest to get silently wrong: a single tuple would make every succession witness invalid, the reducer would answer ILLEGAL_TRANSITION, and the refusal tests would pass while the positive path was dead. Drill (e) targets exactly that and must redden a POSITIVE test.

`validSuccessionBinding` is exported and requires exact(SUCCESSION_KEYS) + hex64 predecessor content hash + non-empty predecessorRevisionId + safe-integer predecessorGraphEpoch >= 1. The `>= 1` floor matters: epoch 0 means "never activated", so a succession claiming to replace an epoch-0 predecessor is unverifiable and refuses.

`validActivationEpoch` holds the arithmetic. Deliberate detail: it branches on `"succession" in value`, NOT on `succession === undefined`. Under exactOptionalPropertyTypes a witness could still arrive from untyped input with the key present and the value undefined; the `in` test sends that down the succession branch, where `validSuccessionBinding(undefined)` is false and it refuses. The `=== undefined` form would have silently re-classified it as an initial activation and accepted it at epoch 1. Fail closed either way, no default.

Rules: no succession -> epoch EXACTLY 1. Succession -> epoch EXACTLY predecessorGraphEpoch + 1. Non-integer/NaN/absent -> false before either branch.

`validGraphEpochPlacement` at the state layer (now :123-130) is untouched as instructed -- it governs where a bound epoch may exist on STATE (>= 1 for ACTIVE/SUPERSEDED, exactly 0 otherwise) and remains correct; the new rules govern the COMMAND witness. The two layers are complementary, not duplicated.

THREE NEW EXPORTS, all derived from production output rather than hand-built:
